# frontier-wire

> An openly automated, bilingual (RU + EN) news wire covering AI, tech, science, world and culture.
> Written twice a day by a scheduled agent from real, cited sources. Everything is open:
> the source list, the pipeline, and every edition as plain markdown.

Publisher: Danila Katalshov — https://adanman.github.io

## Machine-friendly entry points
- RSS feed: https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/feed.xml
- JSON Feed (with raw-markdown pointers): https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/feed.json
- Latest edition, plain markdown index: https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/latest.md
- Sitemap: https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/sitemap.xml
- Raw markdown of every article: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ADanMan/frontier-wire/main/editions/<YYYY>/<MM-DD>/<NN-slug>.md
- Source list (RSS feeds we read): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ADanMan/frontier-wire/main/feeds.txt
- Edition format spec: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ADanMan/frontier-wire/main/FORMAT.md
- Repository: https://github.com/ADanMan/frontier-wire

## Latest articles
- [One symptom, three levers": a new paper questions a trendy way to fine-tune AI models](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-09/01-on-policy-self-distillation-critique.html) — A new arXiv paper takes apart on-policy self-distillation, a popular way to fine-tune language models on their own output, and promises to trace its problems to one shared symptom and three possible fixes.
- [Scientists are teaching AI to spot change in satellite images — the real bottleneck is the images themselves](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-09/02-remote-sensing-change-synthesis.html) — A new paper proposes generating synthetic before-and-after satellite image pairs guided by real-world knowledge instead of handwritten rules, to train models that track change on Earth's surface.
- [OpenAI says an AI solved the $1 million Navier-Stokes problem. Mathematicians are arguing over who gets credit](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-09/03-navier-stokes-ai-proof-controversy.html) — An unreleased OpenAI model and 10,000 AI agents reportedly cracked one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems in 88 hours — and immediately triggered a fight over credit.
- [The head of the Smithsonian Institution is stepping down after 38 years](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-09/04-smithsonian-bunch-retires.html) — Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie G. Bunch III has announced his retirement — a career at the institution that began in the 1970s and whose biggest legacy is the National Museum of African American History and Culture.
- [Thieves stole $2.5 million in Renoir paintings from a French museum — then dropped half of them while fleeing](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-09/05-renoir-museum-heist.html) — Burglars took four paintings from the Renoir Museum on the French Riviera and dropped two of them during their escape.
- [In China, lawyers, architects, and engineers are moonlighting to teach AI their own professions](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-09/06-china-gig-ai-trainers.html) — Amid a sluggish economy and state directives, underemployed Chinese professionals are taking cheap gig work teaching AI the expertise of their own trades — just to cover the mortgage.
- [Scientists found proteins in rattlesnake blood that neutralize venom 10 times more effectively than current antidotes](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-09/07-rattlesnake-antivenom.html) — Combinations of toxin-blocking proteins from rattlesnake blood outperformed a commercial antivenom in lab tests — and worked against venom from several dangerous species at once.
- [Microsoft just patched a record 972 vulnerabilities in one Patch Tuesday — 112 of them critical](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-09/08-microsoft-patch-tuesday-record.html) — Ars Technica calls the latest Microsoft update batch a "doozy" — the biggest patch volume on record, driven partly by the threat of AI-assisted attacks.
- [NASA's Curiosity rover just logged 5,000 Martian days on Mars — and became a record-setting climber along the way](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-09/09-curiosity-5000-martian-days.html) — NASA's latest Curiosity mission blog says the rover has passed 5,000 sols on Mars — and along the way climbed higher than any other Mars rover has gone.
- [Stealing candy from kids, splash-proof urinals, and buried underwear win the 2026 Ig Nobel Prizes](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-09/10-ig-nobel-prizes-2026.html) — Smithsonian Magazine rounds up this year's Ig Nobel Prize winners — the spoof award for real research that's funny first and thought-provoking second.
- [A new giant dinosaur turned up beneath a construction site in Brazil — as long as a city block](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-09/11-brazil-giant-dinosaur.html) — Scientists have described a newly identified dinosaur roughly 20 meters long that lived 120 million years ago — and found an unexpected evolutionary link to a dinosaur from Spain.
- [Hurricane Lowell slams Hawaii's western islands, knocking out power to 91% of one island](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-09/12-hurricane-lowell-hawaii.html) — Hurricane Lowell battered Hawaii with damaging winds, heavy rain, and flooding and is pushing further into the Pacific, having knocked out power to nearly all of one western island.
- [LG TVs caught scanning home networks for other people's phones and devices](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-09/13-lg-tv-lan-tracking.html) — Ars Technica reports on a demonstration showing LG televisions scanning the local network for other devices — and, apparently, capable of tracking user activity even while offline.
- [The "water thief": how an ancient Greek water clock stayed the most accurate way to measure time for 1,800 years](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-09/14-ancient-greek-water-clock.html) — Open Culture traces the history of the clepsydra — ancient Greece's water clock, with roots reaching back at least to the 16th century BCE.
- [Microsoft's tool that turns office files into Markdown just shot up GitHub's trending list](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-08/01-microsoft-markitdown-trending.html) — The markitdown repo climbed to #2 on today's GitHub trending list with 771 stars in a day — a familiar pattern for tools that prep documents for AI pipelines.
- [HeyGen built a tool that writes HTML and renders it as video — made for AI agents](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-08/02-heygen-hyperframes.html) — The hyperframes repo topped today's GitHub trending list with 734 stars in a day — an agent writes HTML markup, and the tool renders it straight into video.
- [AI agents are drowning in context — a new tool claims a 98% cut](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-08/03-context-mode-agent-tooling.html) — The context-mode repo landed at #3 on today's GitHub trending list — it sandboxes an agent's tool output and claims a 98% cut in what ends up in the context window, across 17 platforms.
- [Researchers get AI to understand speech and video together without retraining a thing](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-08/04-speech-centric-omni-understanding.html) — A new paper links speech, on-screen events, and their timing using off-the-shelf, "frozen" vision-language models — with no additional training at all.
- [An avatar that talks and moves at once — from one model, not two](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-08/05-motion-omni-avatar-dialogue.html) — A new paper called Motion-Omni merges speech generation and full-body motion for a talking avatar into a single model — a job previously split across separate systems.
- [GitHub's trending list has a "stealth" browser built for AI agents — one that gets past Cloudflare](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-08/06-camofox-stealth-browser.html) — The camofox-browser repo landed at #4 on today's GitHub trending list with 285 stars in a day — a headless browser built to look like a regular user to anti-bot systems.
